sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Urban Electric Cargo Bicycles and Step-Through Scooters

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified system with Napoleonic heritage; Islamic Sharia is a principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–EU Association Agreement (2004, including investment liberalization provisions)
Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab States (1980)
Egypt–United States Trade and Investment Framework Agreement (1999)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Laws No. 36 of 2014, No. 8 of 2015 and No. 154 of 2019, together with its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree); Central Bank of Egypt KYC/AML rules; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (GAFI UBO declaration filings).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (UBO data is filed with GAFI and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) and is not publicly searchable; regulated entities receive UBO information under mandatory CDD obligations only)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention in force in Egypt since 14 December 2022); consular legalization by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (statutes) of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent ministries of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of each foreign corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and appointing its signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate board of directors (resolution certified by the corporate secretary and notarized in the country of origin)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports of all UBOs, directors and managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent public registry in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian consular legalization (or certification by the Egyptian Embassy for foreign-domiciled persons)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation attorney (executed before a notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution or Egyptian consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers and authorized signatories against the EMLCU consolidated terrorism lists (implementing UNSCR 1267/1988 and applicable UN Security Council sanctions), the Central Bank of Egypt designations, the OFAC SDN List (mandatory for the USD SWIFT LC and TT wire clearing rails), and the EU consolidated sanctions list. Law No. 80 of 2002 requires risk-based customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), and retention of UBO identification records for five years following termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) one-stop-shop electronic name reservation service (www.gafi.gov.eg), integrated with the National Commercial Registry system managed by the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be registered in Arabic. The statutory name formula is: an Arabic word denoting 'Company', followed by the object of incorporation, followed by a distinctive personal or trade word. Latin-script transliteration is not the legal corporate name; an English rendering may be recorded alongside the Arabic name for banking and customs purposes only.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Name of any foreign state or sovereign symbol
Words contrary to public order or misleading to the public
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 business days of a name rejection, the incorporator may file a written reconsideration request with the GAFI Registration (Name) Committee. A further administrative appeal lies to the GAFI Chairman within 30 days. Final administrative decisions are judicially reviewable before the Council of State (Administrative Court) within 60 days of notification. The applicant may simultaneously submit alternative name proposals to avoid procedural delay; a rejected name file may be reopened without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for this manufacturing scope: ISIC 3091 requires a physical lease (notarized and stamp-taxed) plus an industrial operating license from the Industrial Development Authority (IDA) for a production premises with civil-defense, health and environmental approvals; virtual/receptionist office services cannot satisfy the factory license, environmental or civil-defense inspection criteria.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — quantified risk of 0.75 (75%): at least one unannounced on-site inspection by the Industrial Development Authority, civil defense or environmental authority within the first 12 months of industrial operation; GAFI also performs a registered-address verification visit during the initial registration cycle.

Notarization and stamp duty for the registered office lease

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and unified with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; particularly Articles 82–103 governing Limited Liability Companies before the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department, One-Stop Shop, in coordination with the Commercial Registry at the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (combined constitutional deed) filed electronically through the GAFI e-Service platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital threshold is imposed for an LLC under Law 159/1981 as amended, provided the nominal capital is divided into equal quotas. The declared cash capital must be fully subscribed and paid into a blocked temporary escrow account at a licensed Egyptian bank; the bank maintains the freeze until GAFI issues the initial incorporation certificate and commercial registration is completed. In-kind contributions must be independently valued and transferred to the company before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned founding shareholders of [COMPANY NAME] LLC, having executed the Memorandum and Articles of Association, hereby formally adopt the same and approve the subscription to, and the allotment of, the entire issued share capital in the proportions set forth in the Subscription Schedule; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at [STREET ADDRESS], Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt, and the Company Registrar is directed to file the said address and any subsequent changes with GAFI and the Commercial Registry; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [NAME_A] is appointed General Manager and [NAME_B] is appointed Company Secretary, each to act within the lawful powers delegated by the Board, and the Chair is authorized to execute all statutory registration forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (online via GAFI e-Service portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed company names in Arabic and English; verify non-conflict with existing trademarks and trade names and compliance with Law 159/1981. The reserved name will be evidenced by a GAFI clearance letter valid for sixty days.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney (if a corporate or delegated representative acts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict, file a written appeal with the GAFI Commercial Registry and resubmit a revised set of proposed names; no additional official fee is incurred for one re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Escrow Account Opening for Paid-up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt or any GAFI-approved bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked escrow account in the future company name; deposit the full cash paid-up capital; obtain a certificate of deposit confirming the amount is frozen until GAFI releases the funds upon issuance of commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Signatory specimens and board resolution if a corporate founder is involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC documentation, provide the requested corporate ownership chart and source-of-funds confirmation; resubmit within ten business days to avoid cancellation of the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary Bureau or GAFI-authorized notarization officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders or their authorized representatives must appear physically or through a lawful electronic notarization session to sign the Memorandum and Articles of Association; the notary verifies identity and legal capacity and affixes notarial certification.
required_dossiers: Completed MoA and AoA in Arabic
Passports and national IDs of signatories
Registered office lease agreement (validated for notarial purposes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies discrepancies between the submitted draft and the bilingual corporate data, execute a corrective addendum and re-present the document for notarization within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department – E-Service Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized incorporation deed, bank deposit certificate, registered office lease, and founder identification records to the GAFI e-service system; pay the statutory filing fee, notarization stamping fees, and publication contribution through the centralized e-payment gateway.
required_dossiers: Founder passport copies and national IDs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a clarification query or rejection, submit a written response together with the requested rectification documents within fifteen working days; the application remains pending if unanswered beyond that period and must be resubmitted with payment of the re-evaluation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration in the Trade Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop with delegation to the Ministry of Trade and Industry Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After GAFI issues the initial incorporation certificate, the same dossier is registered in the official Commercial Registry; the authority issues a commercial registration extract and publishes the establishment notice in the official gazette.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the lease agreement
Power of attorney for the registration representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry rejects or suspends the registration, cure by rectifying the registered office description or the object clauses, pay any minor correction fees, and file a formal request for reinstatement through the GAFI One-Stop Shop.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card and Value-Added Tax Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Taxpayer Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for a tax card within the legal deadline from commercial registration; complete VAT enrollment if the company expects taxable services or goods; obtain a certificate of registration and tax identification number.
required_dossiers: Founder IDs and legal representation forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA queries the business activity or location, provide additional supporting documentation or an updated lease; file an administrative objection with the ETA registration branch and follow up within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the employer entity with NOSI; submit the founding directors/employees list and pay any initial insurance contributions required for the statutory social insurance coverage of employees.
required_dossiers: Employment agreements or worker registration list
National ID copies of all insured personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI disputes the employee count or contribution basis, provide corrected employment records and payroll reconciliations; appeal the preliminary determination to the NOSI regional director within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the GOEIC importer/exporter registry to enable duty-free or bonded importation of batteries, motors, frames, and electronic components; obtain the importer code for customs clearance transactions.
required_dossiers: Company profile and physical address evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GOEIC withholds registration due to industrial license status, first obtain the Industrial Development Authority license, then file a supplementary application for GOEIC registration; or request interim import clearance under customs bond.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) – Ministry of Trade and Industry, Central Sector for Industrial Permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Establishment Operating License under Law No. 15 of 2017 on Industrial Permits and its Executive Regulations No. 729 of 2018

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Limited Environmental Impact / Simplified Environmental Examination. The electric cargo bicycle and scooter assembly facility requires an Environmental Management Plan (EMP) and, because battery assembly is included, a reduced Environmental and Occupational Risk Assessment. No full EIA report is mandated unless the facility conducts painting or electroplating using hazardous chemicals, in which case a screening scoping study is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with Law 4/1994 and Decree 44/2000 limits to public sewer: pH 6–9.5, BOD ≤ 600 mg/L, COD ≤ 900 mg/L, TSS ≤ 400 mg/L, oil & grease ≤ 100 mg/L, and lead ≤ 1 mg/L. VOC stack emissions from painting and powder-coating lines shall not exceed 30 mg/m³. Hazardous waste (e.g., spent lithium cells, solvents, waste paint) must be separated, labeled, and disposed of through EEAA-licensed carriers using a manifest tracking system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance under Civil Defense Law No. 930 of 1969 shall be obtained after inspection of fire extinguishers, emergency exits, a sprinkler or alarm system, and safe storage of lithium-ion batteries in fire-resistant cabinets. Occupational Safety and Health clearance from the Ministry of Manpower under Law No. 12 of 2003 requires structural load inspections for production equipment, compliance with electrical grounding and mechanical guarding regimes, and submission of a workplace hazard assessment, training plan, and first aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoicing and tax registration platform: https://www.inatax.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Egyptian LLCs obtain a statutory Tax Identification Number by submitting to the competent local tax office an application for the Unified Tax Card together with the commercial registry extract, articles of association, proof of paid-in capital, board resolution appointing signatories, power of attorney, passports/commercial records of shareholders, lease or title documents for the registered premises, and a bank certificate for the Egyptian corporate account. VAT registration is effected through the ETA InTax portal, which activates the VAT account, withholding tax account, and e-invoice/e-receipt profiles upon verification of the tax card. Foreign entities without a physical Egyptian establishment may obtain a non-resident taxpayer ID for withholding and invoicing purposes through the International Tax department of the ETA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not maintain a US-style check-the-box or fiscal transparency election. An LLC is unconditionally treated as a separate taxable entity under Corporate Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 at a headline rate of 22.5% (industrial/commercial profits). Permitted statutory elections are limited to (i) VAT grouping/reverse-charge election for related parties under Law No. 67 of 2016, (ii) the small-business cash-basis election within the threshold set by ministerial decree, and (iii) investment-incentive elections under the Unified Investment Law including accelerated depreciation and the 50% capital expenditure deduction for qualifying projects. Hybrid mismatch elections under BEPS Action 2 are not domesticated in Egypt.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 in annual taxable turnover, mandating compulsory VAT registration; exporters and companies carrying on taxable activities may apply for voluntary registration below the threshold in accordance with Article 17 of Law No. 67 of 2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B and B2G invoices, and receipts issued by tax-registered persons, must be transmitted in real time to the ETA InTax fiscal-clearance platform using the approved JSON/XML schema. The system performs automated validation of tax IDs, invoice stamps, invoice sequence, and computation before returning a compliant invoice bearing a digital signature, unique cleared UID, and QR code embedding receipt and VAT data. Un-cleared invoices are treated as never issued, denying input VAT recovery to the buyer and exposing the seller to administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating is available for the supply of goods exported by the tax-registered manufacturer provided the goods are actually removed from Egypt, the exporter retains proof of shipment and payment, and the bank receives the hard-currency proceeds within the statutory repatriation window. Direct export of electric cargo bicycles qualifies automatically; connected offshore services such as warehousing, freight, ancillary logistics, or after-sales support supplied to non-resident buyers are zero-rated when consumed entirely abroad and supported by contracts and invoicing records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Single Administrative Document showing dispatch from Egyptian Customs territory
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing departure
Inward Remittance Certificate from an Egyptian licensed bank proving receipt of foreign-currency sale proceeds
Zero-rated e-invoice cleared through the InTax platform
Certificate of Origin and commercial invoice
Proof of VAT registration and the export contract for desk-audit matching
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to desk and field audit by the ETA with a general 5-year limitation period, extended to 6 years in cases of willful misdeclaration. If the ETA determines that export documentation is fabricated or that foreign proceeds were not repatriated within 180 days absent a valid Central Bank of Egypt extension, the zero rate is retrospectively rescinded; the exporter is immediately liable for the uncollected 14% VAT, monthly delay surcharges (currently 2% per month), a statutory fine of 50% to 100% of the understated VAT, and possibly criminal penalties including imprisonment for document forgery and tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egyptian Pound (EGP) is fully convertible for current account transactions (trade goods, services, royalties) subject to documentary verification by an authorized bank. Capital account transactions (equity injections, shareholder loans, loan repayments) require compliance with CBE regulations and, for foreign capital establishment, registration with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI). Profit remittance by a foreign-owned LLC is permitted under Law 72/2017 (Investment Law) provided the company has filed annual tax returns, completed statutory audits, and obtained a tax clearance certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority. No mandatory conversion to EGP is imposed on retained foreign currency; banks may require EGP conversion solely to satisfy local tax and payroll obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: CBE Circular No. 50/2017 abolished the mandatory surrender ratio for export proceeds. For manufactured goods (ISIC 3091), export receipts must be repatriated and physically credited to an authorized bank account in Egypt within 120 days from the bill of lading date. Up to 100% of the receipts may be retained in a foreign currency account; conversion to EGP is at the exporter's discretion, except that banks may require EGP conversion to cover local statutory payments (taxes, social insurance, salaries) in the absence of an approved plan for using foreign currency for direct import obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (temporary foreign investment account under the Companys Law) / Operational Foreign Currency Account
Operational EGP and USD Account / Trade Finance Line (LC and wire)
Operational EGP and USD Account / Import LC Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licences confer no automatic recognition in Egypt. Any non-bank entity providing payment accounts or cross-border clearing must be licensed by the CBE under Law 194/2020 and obtain a payment system operator authorisation. In practice, CBE-authorised fintechs (e.g., local payment platforms) may provide a limited scope of cash management services, but a foreign EMI cannot legally hold corporate EGP accounts or open settlement accounts in Egypt. Full cross-border banking services remain tied to CBE-regulated commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for corporate onboarding. All authorized signatories and each ultimate beneficial owner of the EG_LLC must appear before the bank's CBE-designated compliance officer in person in Egypt (at the branch). Remote video verification is not accepted for first-time onboarding; if a director resides abroad, the power-of-attorney document must be legalised at the relevant Egyptian embassy or consulate, and the attorney-in-fact must attend the branch in person with the original legalised POA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership ambiguity – multiple non-resident shareholders with equal holdings, nominee shareholding suspected.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the LLC's Commercial Registry extract (electronic, dated within 90 days), Articles of Association indicating actual economic owners, GAFI incorporation certificate, and a formal UBO declaration in the bank's prescribed form, supported by passports and proof of address for each UBO. If nominee holdings are used, a notarised nominee trust deed must be submitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of initial capital injection (e.g., large equity transfer from a tax-haven jurisdiction).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or bank statements of the investors for the last 12 months, sale and purchase agreement at the time of capital formation, or a gift/inheritance deed where applicable; anti-money-laundering source-of-funds questionnaire; and, if the amount exceeds USD 500,000, a formal independent audit trail certified by a licensed external auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border trade with low-duty jurisdictions or use of unverified freight-forwarding counterparts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and final commercial invoices from end buyers; bill of lading / airway bill copies; customs export declarations (including HS code 8711.60 for electric bicycles); a copy of the underlying trade contract; and due-diligence files on major suppliers and logistics agents (e.g., UAE intermediate broker, if applicable) to demonstrate a legitimate commercial purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment (equity) must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with the CBE Transaction Purpose Code 171 (Other direct investment – shares). The paying bank must reference the GAFI approval number and the unique investment file (Investor Account) in the wire message's remittance information field (field 70). The receiving Egyptian bank is required to obtain a CBE automated proof of investment importation before crediting an Operational Account. If using the temporary Capital Escrow Account, the bank will open this sub-account under the auspices of the General Authority for Investment and request the CBE's approval (Form A) before conversion or onward use; all funds must be parked for a minimum of 7 business days while KYC and sanctions screening are completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for imported components (batteries, electric motors, controllers) should be executed as (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for invoices below USD 100,000, using CBE Transaction Purpose Code 150 (General trade – import of goods), with an invoice, bill of lading, and a customs import declaration attached; or (ii) Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) for larger orders, issued by the Egyptian bank in favour of the supplier, with 90-day tenor permissible to match cash-conversion cycle. The L/C must include the CBE's SWIFT code and be advised through a correspondent bank; Egyptian banks will require the common EBC (Exchange Control Form No. 1) for every outward remittance, signed by the company's authorised signatory and stamped by the compliance department. Payment under L/C is released against presentation of the full transport and quality inspection documents, and Customs Authority approval is mandatory before the foreign exchange settlement is wired out.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (onshore EGP/USD) with tenors up to 12 months, executed through an authorised Egyptian bank and requiring an underlying trade transaction or invoice.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP) with tenor aligned to export receivables, subject to CBE's digitle settlement via SAMA-CBE portal (if available) and regulatory margin requirement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) traded with authorised offshore counterparties, approved by the CBE’s Balance of Payments department; settlement is made in USD against the spot reference rate published by the CBE, used only for hedging expected export income.
Plain-vanilla FX options (call USD / put EGP) bought from onshore banks with a clear hedging rationale and zero premium leakage; covered in the company’s risk management policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Egyptian Tax Form No. 1) together with audited financial statements and statutory books prepared for the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Taxpayer Services Center with jurisdiction over the company's address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than four months after the fiscal year end; for a 31 December year-end, filing due before 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed late-filing penalty of EGP 500–5,000 (roughly USD 10–100), additional tax at 2% per month on unpaid tax for late payment, asset attachment, and initiation of criminal sanctions for knowingly false declarations; persistent default may lead the Commercial Registry to list the entity as non-compliant and eventually to administrative strike-off after repeated warnings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved audited financial statements, annual general assembly minutes, and the manager/auditor report filed with the corporate registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Corporate Registry Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General assembly must be convened within six months of balance sheet date, i.e., on or before 30 June for a 31 December year-end; minutes filed with GAFI within 30 days after the assembly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance fines against responsible managers up to EGP 50,000 (roughly USD 1,000); GAFI may reject subsequent administrative transactions, issue a formal compliance notice, and initiate administrative strike-off if corrective filings are not made within 90 days.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of commercial-registration particulars, statutory register integrity, and direct plus ultimate beneficial-ownership statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Supply, with information filed simultaneously in the GAFI AML/CFT beneficial-owner database
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each year, and within 30 days of any change to directors/managers, shareholders, registered office, or beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delay fee of EGP 1,000 (approx. USD 20) for late beneficial-owner confirmation; false declarations attract fines up to EGP 100,000 (approx. USD 2,000) and imprisonment of the responsible manager; unremedied defects trigger deregistration and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual economic activity / industrial operating-status declaration accompanying audited statements for the manufacturing license file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) with copy to GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 1 July of the year following the reporting period or 60 days after the GAFI annual filing, whichever arrives earlier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative fee of EGP 2,000–10,000 (approx. USD 40–200); IDA may suspend the industrial license and the facility's operational approvals for up to 150 days before recommending strike-off of the underlying LLC.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified-public-accountant audit is mandatory when paid-in share capital exceeds EGP 200,000 (approx. USD 4,000), when one or more partners holding at least 10% request an audit, or when gross annual turnover exceeds EGP 1,000,000 (approx. USD 20,000); manufacturing LLCs under Investment Law 72/2017 are also audited as a licensing condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) consolidated under Ministry of Finance Decree 110/2015 and in line with the Financial Regulatory Authority guidance; EAS are fully consistent with IFRS for material statutory filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Per Egypt AML Law 80/2002 and amendments by Law 83/2019, the LLC must maintain a register of direct senior managing officials and beneficial owners, identify individuals owning or controlling over 10% ultimately, and file or confirm this register annually; any equity transfer or voting-right change requires a refreshed UBO declaration to GAFI within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors/Managers (including managers of the LLC)
Minute Book of general and management meetings
Statutory accounting books and supporting voucher folder

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–1,200 per year for registered agent, local office services and registered-address base in Cairo or Suez Canal Economic Zone
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–4,500 per year for a low-risk manufacturing LLC with audited financial statements and tax-file attachments.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% standard corporate income tax (CIT) on net taxable income of Egyptian juridical persons under the Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended by Law No. 30 of 2023; expressly applicable to an Egyptian Limited Liability Company (LLC) engaged in ISIC 3091 manufacture of urban electric cargo bicycles.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 1) SME preferential regime (Law No. 152 of 2020, as amended): an LLC with annual gross turnover not exceeding EGP 20,000,000 may irrevocably elect a gross-turnover tax at graduated rates of 0.5% (first EGP 1,000,000 tranche), 1.25% (next EGP 9,000,000 tranche) and 2.5% (next EGP 10,000,000 tranche) for a five-year lock period, wholly substituting the 22.5% net-income basis. 2) Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Suez Canal Economic Zone Law No. 83 of 2015 incentives: a qualifying newly established electric e-bike manufacturing project inside an approved investment zone or the SCZone may obtain a five-year CIT exemption, accelerated depreciation, and reduced customs duties of up to 50% on imported capital equipment and assembly-line machinery. 3) Standard deductions remain available: inventory and production costs, wages, utilities, bank LC fees, insurance, research and quality-control costs, and a foreign tax credit for treaty-sourced income.
